target.name: Makemake
target.blurb: One of the brightest worlds in the Kuiper Belt, a dwarf planet covered in methane ice.

warnings: The spectrum is not typed: the brown-dwarf templates do not apply to a Solar System body, which shines by reflected sunlight.
credits: SPHEREx DR1/QR3 spectral images, NASA/JPL-Caltech via NASA/IPAC IRSA
Solar reference: CALSPEC sun_mod_001 (Bohlin, Gordon & Tremblay 2014, PASP 126, 711)

solar_system.composition: methane ice dominates, with strong CH4 bands through the near-infrared (Grundy et al. 2024, JWST NIRSpec, arXiv:2309.05085)

skipped_passes.reason: fewer than 6 exposures contain the body

body_frames.note: Each exposure resampled on a grid centred on the body at its own time: the body stays at the centre and background stars trail.

solar_system.method: Forced ePSF photometry at the JPL Horizons position (seen from SPHEREx) in every exposure; errors scaled by the scatter at 8 empty positions per frame. Controls: the same photometry at 8 track positions in the body's other passes, when it is degrees away; the body flux is body minus control per detector band. Reflectance: flux divided by the CALSPEC solar model averaged over each channel, normalised over 0.75-1.3 um. Band depth: 1 - (mean reflectance in band / mean over 0.75-1.3 um).
